text: You can think of T3 Code as an open source "bring-your-own-subscription" alternative to apps like Claude Desktop, Codex App, Cursor, Glass and Conductor.
We have over 100,000 users who love T3 Code.
Lots of apps have gotten bogged down with bad tech decisions and "slop". We have not, and we're proud of the performance of T3 Code.

We regularly audit for performance regressions, often caused by sending too much data over websockets, css animations causing gpu spikes, lists being hard to render, and more. Make sure all changes are considerate of performance impact
T3 Code has 3 key app surfaces: web, desktop, and mobile.

text: The character animations look horrible. Use better animations from Mixamo for sprinting and jumping, as if the character is leaning forward like a ninja and moving really quickly. After each completed attempt at rerigging the character, a separate critic agent (a brutal AAA art director who writes no code) takes its own screenshots from several points in time of the animation and scores the aesthetics from 0–10: 8–5 = amazing, really professional quality, 7 = ok but still rigid, 5 = too rigid and fake. Pass = ≥8.5 with zero errors. Below that the builder gets the ranked issue list and tries again, up to 4 rounds.
Also, add more effects and elements for camera motion when I move the character around. It should look visually impressive and not just a rigid 3D animation.

I'll replace the procedural sprint and jump clips with Mixamo motion, then tune the camera and movement effects around them. I'll have a separate critic inspect animation samples across time after each attempt, for up to four rounds.
Used Chrome and the Browser, ran commands

Mixamo is accessible in your logged-in Chrome session. I'm downloading its captured running motion at full keyframe quality, then I'll retarget it to Butterfly's rig and separate the jump, airtime, and landing behavior so jumps don't repeat a single stiff pose.
